data.narrative:
Valar Atomics, a Series G nuclear energy company founded by Isaiah P. Taylor, is evaluated against a comp universe of 8 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private firms (Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, ARC Clean Technology). The company has raised $149M to date.

The valuation analysis applies one quantitative method: stage-progression triangulation. Using total capital raised ($149M) as a proxy anchor of $6.0B, a typical Series G step-up multiplier of 1.25x yields an implied valuation of $7.5B. A peer-median approach was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear energy sector; only four same-sector peers exist, with none meeting the narrow-filter thresholds required for statistical reliability.

The triangulated valuation range is $6.4B (low), $7.5B (median), and $8.6B (high), derived from stage-progression alone. The principal uncertainty is the absence of robust private-market peer pricing at Series G within nuclear energy, which limits cross-validation of the step-up multiplier. Additional sensitivity would benefit from public-market trading multiples (EV/revenue or deployed-capital metrics) on the three public comparables, though such data was not provided. Until adjacent-stage nuclear peers achieve comparable scale or disclosure, this range reflects limited triangulation and should be treated as preliminary.
